ticket: JSRT-20 (JsObject property store O(1) access) + JSRT-21 WIP (array set path)

jsrt20.root_cause: crates/amazing-js/src/value.rs JsObject.props was a linear-scan Vec<(PropertyKey, Property)>; get_own/own_prop/define/delete_own/own_slot_index all did a full .iter().find()/.position() scan, so single-property access was O(n) and building an n-property object was O(n^2).
jsrt20.fix: Added prop_index: HashMap<PropertyKey, usize> as a purely additive side index alongside the existing insertion-ordered Vec (never tombstoned/compacted, so slot indices used by vm/fast_path.rs's inline caches stay stable). Rewrote get_own/own_prop/define/delete_own/own_slot_index to O(1) lookups via prop_index; added push_prop() helper for the two append sites (initialize_string_data, array()'s initial length push). own_property_keys's spec ordering (integer indices ascending, then strings insertion order, then symbols insertion order) and define()'s shape_version bump semantics (bump on new-key add, or on an existing key's attribute change, never on a pure value update) are unchanged.
jsrt20.scope_note: Kept entirely inside value.rs and its direct accessors per the ticket's explicit constraint, since js-lang/js-vm were landing large changes concurrently.

microbenchmark.note: Full-spec-size (100k object / 1M array) run against the OLD linear-scan store is computationally impractical (O(n^2)); measured a bounded scaling trend instead, then ran AFTER at the full ticket-specified size.

before_release_bounded.scaling_10x_step: ~93x (object), ~89x (push), ~70x (index-assign) for a 10x size increase, confirming O(n^2)

after_release_full_spec_size.caveat: Runs were on venus-001/venus-003 under varying concurrent load from other lanes (observed load average up to 32 on one run); numbers are directionally consistent but not isolated single-tenant measurements.

jsrt21_wip.status: in progress, not the ticket this evidence file gates -- included here because its 3 commits sit in the same tree this gate measured

item_1_redundant_lookups.root_cause: set_with_receiver's fallback (builtins_std_object_model.rs) built a throwaway JsObject descriptor and round-tripped it through define_own_property, which re-parses each field via std_descriptor_fields (has_property+get_prop per field) and re-fetches the same own-property `existing` set_with_receiver had already looked up. set_prop (interp_property_access.rs) called own_prop(&key) twice back-to-back with nothing mutating the object in between, and refetched "length" twice per array-index write.
item_1_redundant_lookups.fix: Added ordinary_set_data_property, reusing the already-fetched property/length directly. Merged set_prop's duplicate fetches, keeping a re-fetch only around the "length" ToNumber conversion (a hostile valueOf can mutate/delete the property as a side effect there).

item_2_proxy_trap_bug_fixed.root_cause: ordinary_set_data_property skipped the window_proxy_define/proxy_define trap checks define_own_property makes on entry, so setting through a Proxy or WindowProxy silently used the ordinary algorithm instead of invoking the trap.
item_2_proxy_trap_bug_fixed.fix: Falls back to the general descriptor-based path only when the target actually is a Proxy or WindowProxy (checked via is_window_proxy/proxy_parts); the common ordinary-object case still takes the fast path.

item_3_array_length_truncation_bug_fixed.root_cause: ordinary_set_data_property's existing-property branch wrote .value through for every property, including an Array's "length", which is exotic even under plain [[Set]]: shrinking it must delete elements at or above the new length (ArraySetLength, 10.4.2.1). The general path got this via define_own_property's own "is_array && key == length" branch; the fast path skipped straight to a value write and lost it. arr.length = x (Reference::Property assignment, interp_stmt.rs) and Object.assign onto an array both go through this path.
item_3_array_length_truncation_bug_fixed.caught_by: Direct per-file diff against .agents/test262/baseline.json (6a002829): built-ins/Array lost 56 passes (length/* and the ES5 15.4.5.1/15.4.5.2-numbered corpus), built-ins/Object lost 1 (Object/assign/target-Array.js). Same root cause for both.
item_3_array_length_truncation_bug_fixed.fix: Restored ToNumber + range validation + array_prepare_length_change before writing the new length, matching define_own_property's original special case.

gate.platform: Linux (venus-003 for corpus + workspace, venus-001 for crate-scoped iteration)
gate.before_source: .agents/test262/baseline.json (6a002829 full run from origin/dev), same timeout_seconds so directly comparable

built-ins/RegExp/property-escapes.note: No meaningful change (421->419 timeouts). The ticket's hypothesis named two mechanisms, buildString() and .apply() over big arrays; JSRT-20 fixes the O(n) property-access path that .apply()'s create_list_from_array_like relies on, but buildString()-style repeated string concatenation is a separate JsString-immutability cost this ticket did not touch. Flagged as a known gap, not claimed as fixed.

workspace.doctests: all ok across the workspace; amazing_js 1 passed, amazing_html 1 passed (the two crates with real doctests), all others 0 passed/ok

crate_amazing_js.nextest: 445 tests run: 445 passed, 1 skipped (venus-001, with the two JSRT-21 fixups applied)

known_gaps: built-ins/RegExp/property-escapes timeouts are essentially unchanged (421 -> 419); the dominant cost there is very likely JsString concatenation (buildString()-style repeated += on an immutable Rc<[u16]>), not property access. Candidate for a follow-up ticket, out of JSRT-20's value.rs-only scope.

JSRT-21's own micro-benchmark (push/index-assign per-element cost) did not show a clear, isolated improvement in this session's measurements -- runs were contended with other lanes' concurrent builds on shared venus hosts (observed load average up to 32). The redundant-lookup removal is behavior-preserving and gate-clean, but its performance impact needs a re-measurement on an idle host before being reported as a win.
